patch:
diff --git a/changelog.d/1593.change.md b/changelog.d/1593.change.md
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..481dcb7
--- /dev/null
+++ b/changelog.d/1593.change.md
@@ -0,0 +1 @@
+`ClassVar` annotations are now correctly detected when they come back as forward references (e.g. on Python 3.14+, where unresolvable annotations are returned as `ForwardRef` objects instead of strings).
diff --git a/src/attr/_make.py b/src/attr/_make.py
index 04104d9..69a5ac3 100644
--- a/src/attr/_make.py
+++ b/src/attr/_make.py
@@ -297,7 +297,7 @@ def _is_class_var(annot):
     annotations which would put attrs-based classes at a performance
     disadvantage compared to plain old classes.
     """
-    annot = str(annot)
+    annot = str(getattr(annot, "__forward_arg__", annot))
 
     # Annotation can be quoted.
     if annot.startswith(("'", '"')) and annot.endswith(("'", '"')):
diff --git a/tests/test_annotations.py b/tests/test_annotations.py
index e193d4b..780058e 100644
--- a/tests/test_annotations.py
+++ b/tests/test_annotations.py
@@ -691,10 +691,12 @@ class TestAnnotations:
         "typing.ClassVar",
         "'typing.ClassVar[dict]'",
         "t.ClassVar[int]",
+        typing.ForwardRef("typing.ClassVar[int]"),
     ],
 )
 def test_is_class_var(annot):
     """
-    ClassVars are detected, even if they're a string or quoted.
+    ClassVars are detected, even if they're a string, quoted, or a forward
+    reference.
     """
     assert _is_class_var(annot)
